National Weather Service Albuquerque NM
451 PM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Issued at 444 PM MST Mon Nov 16 2026
 
- Patchy fog will create hazardous driving conditions along and 
  just east of the central mountain chain tonight through tomorrow
  morning.

- Snow showers will develop in the northern mountains above 9,000
  feet Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday morning. Slick driving
  conditions may develop on mountain passes.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(This evening through Tuesday night)
Issued at 1239 PM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

Fairly similar conditions exist out in the Land of Enchantment today 
compared to yesterday at this time. Fog has diminished across our 
area, but low clouds firmly remain across portions of eastern NM. 
This will help keep high temperatures once again in the high 40s to 
low 50s, with locations escaping the cloud cover getting into the 
mid 50s. West of the central mountain chain, calm conditions remain 
with only a few passing high clouds. Temperatures are likely to be 
in the high 50s to low 60s. Low clouds and fog look primed to 
develop once again tonight. However, on a fog front, a more robust 
surface pressure gradient in response to an approaching trough will 
increase winds across eastern NM tonight. Thus, fog is increasingly 
less likely in areas that exceed 10mph in winds (which will be much 
of eastern NM, as winds are forecast to be 15-30mph with gusts up to 
40mph, especially in northeast NM). The exception to this is favored 
to be areas from Ruidoso towards Moriarty and up to Santa Fe just 
along the slopes of the central mountains. This is where fog 
developed last night, and winds are favored to not be as strong in 
these areas. With the low clouds and fog expected overnight, 
temperatures across eastern NM won't drop as low as parts of western 
NM. High 30s to low 40s are likely across eastern NM, with mid 30s 
to mid 20s across western NM.

Tuesday brings our first storm system of the week, which is forecast 
to bring breezy conditions across the forecast area, and rain and 
mountain snow to northern NM. The system is forecast to be near Las 
Vegas, NV by midday Tuesday, in which the stronger 700mb winds ahead 
of the trough axis will spread over NM. Across western NM, these 
winds will most likely mix down as they pass over during the 
daytime. In eastern NM, the surface pressure gradient tightens, 
helping aid in strengthening winds even with what likely is less 
mixing from the 700mb level. These south to southwest winds are most 
likely to be in the 20-30mph range with gusts up to 45mph. As the 
system progresses closer to NM, winds taper off across western NM 
outside of higher elevation locations near the Chuska Mountains. In 
northeastern NM, the surface pressure gradient remains strong enough 
for winds to continue through the overnight hours. Wind gusts up to 
55mph may be observed above population centers along the Raton Mesa 
right near the NM/CO border due to the pressure gradient between the 
states.

As the system is pushing through, moisture arrives with it Thursday 
afternoon and evening. As it stands now, rain and mountain snow 
enter western and northwestern NM throughout Tuesday before 
spreading to the northern mountains overnight. As the system pushes 
through, snow likely continues above 9,000ft before snow levels 
decrease as a result of colder 700mb temperatures arriving. However, 
by the time the colder air arrives, precipitation is likely to be 
ending if not already done. Additionally, the path of the system 
continues to trend faster across our area, not leaving much 
residence time for any significant snowfall. Thus, forecast snow 
amounts in the Tusas Mountains have fallen about an inch or so. 
However, we still look most likely to have up to 3-4" fall across 
the higher elevation areas, but most likely to remain above most 
population centers, including Chama. Slick roads may be encountered 
on mountain passes, including Highway 17 north of Chama. Across the 
Sangre de Cristo Mountains, less snowfall is expected as the 
moisture is slated to stay closer to the Tusas Mountains. 
Nevertheless, a few inches of snow cannot be ruled out above 
9,500ft. Snow tapers off by mid-morning Wednesday.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Wednesday through Sunday)
Issued at 1239 PM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

Breezy conditions look to remain across portions of eastern and 
western NM Wednesday afternoon and Thursday, but by and large they
are favored to be quieter weather days as weaker west to 
southwest flow sets up overhead. Temperatures may get up into the 
low to mid 60s across eastern NM by Wednesday due to downsloping 
winds, while western NM will be a day behind due to the passage of
the previous system.

Our next system is forecast to arrive Friday and bring a return of 
winds and precipitation. Currently, winds are favored to be the 
more forthcoming impact, as a robust lee surface trough is 
forecast to develop across southeast CO/northeast NM. 
Concurrently, stronger 700mb winds move across the rest of the 
state during the daytime hours, allowing for those winds to be 
favored to mix to the surface. Overall, winds are currently 
forecast to be stronger than Tuesday's system, though still within
the realm of normalcy in terms of New Mexico windy days. For 
precipitation, model guidance has gradually trended more north 
with the trough axis, which in turn has gradually pushed 
precipitation further into Colorado. As such, significant 
accumulation does not appear likely at this time. Mountain snow 
and low elevation rain looks to be the favored precipitation type 
currently.

After the system passes, models quickly diverge in their solutions, 
which leads to low forecast confidence past Friday. CPC 
precipitation outlooks continue to paint slightly favored chances 
for above normal precipitation across at least our eastern areas 
moving into next week. This makes sense given that even with 
diverging model solutions, global models still paint a more active 
"wave train" of systems moving into western CONUS, which would favor 
us for some unsettled weather.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 444 PM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

MVFR cigs persist in southeast NM this afternoon and will likely
continue through much of the TAF period. Patchy fog will likely
develop again tonight east of the central mountain chain, with the
highlands the favored area. However, a light south breeze could
interfere with the generation of fog, instead favoring low stratus
across much of eastern NM. The REFS is bullish about the
development of low cigs and fog again tonight in portions of
central and northern NM, including west of KAEG and near KSAF,
however NBM probs remain low (<20%) at this time.

A quick-hitting storm will enter into the Four Corners region
Tuesday after 18Z, with showers rapidly spreading from northwest
to southeast. A short period of reduced vis/cigs is expected with
a cold frontal passage and there may be a few lightning strikes
out ahead of the front Tuesday afternoon.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1239 PM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

Critical fire weather conditions are not expected across the next 
several days. However, breezy to windy conditions are forecast for 
Tuesday and Friday. Showers and mountain snow (above 9,000-9,500ft) 
are expected in the northern mountains and adjacent highlands 
Tuesday afternoon into Wednesday morning, with up to 4" of 
accumulation in the Tusas Mountains. Breezy to locally windy 
conditions are forecast Tuesday afternoon across a majority of the 
state (south to southwest winds 15-25mph, with areas in west central 
and northeast NM seeing 20-30mph with gusts up to 40mph). Breezy 
conditions persist Wednesday and Thursday before additional winds 
arrive Friday. Currently, northeast NM is favored for the strongest 
winds with gusts up to 50mph. Elsewhere, winds are favored to gust 
up to 40mph. Rain and mountain snow may reach northwest NM as well, 
though there is lower confidence in this.
